newsitem.title: CANADA: Ranger climbs after takeover report.
newsitem.headline: Ranger climbs after takeover report.

text.p: Shares of Ranger Oil Ltd jumped on Monday after a Canadian newspaper printed a story speculating that the company was a takeover target for Gulf Canada Resources Ltd.
Ranger was up C$0.25 in early Toronto Stock Exchange trade to C$9.75 with 596,300 shares changing hands.
The Financial Post newspaper reported on Saturday that Gulf Canada, which has said it was in the market for an international acquisition, was considering a takeover of Ranger.
Most industry experts -- including Ranger chief executive Fred Dyment -- have agreed that Ranger is viewed as a takeover candidate for several companies inside and outside Canada.
But the odds of Gulf Canada making a play for Ranger, a longtime North Sea producer, were viewed as slim.
"I think that the only people who would buy it would be somebody trying to add to growing North Sea production," said a senior investment industry executive.
"For tax reasons, it makes no sense at all to be a marginal player in the North Sea."

Gulf Canada's current international focus is Indonesia, where it and Talisman Energy Inc are partners in the US$600-million Corridor gas project. Gulf has said it was in the market for another international venture.
Sources also said it was unlikely that Gulf chief executive J. P. Bryan would talk to a national newspaper about an imminent takeover, driving up the target's stock price.

"We've made no secret that we're on the acquisition trail and that we want something international," said Gulf spokesman John Sparks. "So if you take all those statements, it could lead you to Ranger -- it could lead you to 20 other companies."
Ranger beat out Gulf last year in a takeover battle for Czar Resources Ltd, a company both viewed as a strategic fit for their northeast British Columbia natural gas assets.
Gulf backed away from the deal after Ranger raised its offer, saying it showed discipline in not overpaying for acquisitions.
